item.title: 2027: US providing real-time intelligence to Nigerian military against terrorists — Musa
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigeria’s Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa, has said the United States is providing real-time intelligence, satellite imagery and training to the Nigerian military to track and target terrorist leaders ahead of the 2027 general elections. According to Reuters, Musa disclosed this on Monday during a briefing with journalists, saying the improved intelligence support had strengthened the military’s ability to identify and strike militant targets. The minister said Nigerian troops had killed several terrorist and bandit leaders in overnight operations in the Northwest and Northeast, adding that the military was conducting almost daily operations with improved intelligence. “We took out a lot of the bandit leaders and the terrorists themselves,” Musa said. He said Nigeria and the United States had continued to expand their security cooperation as the country battles Islamist insurgencies in the North-East, armed banditry in the North-West and kidnapping gangs across the country. Musa also disclosed that Nigeria was expecting additional military helicopters from the United States and Italy to strengthen its operational capacity. On preparations for the 2027 general elections, the defence minister said security agencies were intensifying intelligence-led operations to prevent violence before, during and after the polls. He said authorities were also monitoring the use of Starlink satellite internet services, cryptocurrencies and commercial drones by militant groups, while working with US authorities to disrupt their financing networks. Musa further disclosed that Nigeria had reached a five-kilometre cross-border right-of-pursuit arrangement with Cameroon, Niger and Chad, allowing troops to pursue terrorists and bandits across border areas. The arrangement is aimed at restricting the movement of armed groups that exploit porous borders to escape security operations. The minister also warned that Islamic State Sahel was seeking to recruit criminal gangs in North-West Nigeria, raising concerns that largely profit-driven bandit groups could develop into ideologically driven insurgent organisations similar to the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP). According to him, militants and bandits have continued to exploit dense forests and porous borders with Niger and Benin to evade security forces after carrying out attacks. However, he said improved surveillance had strengthened the military’s ability to track armed groups through difficult terrain and restricted their freedom of movement. “We don’t want them to develop that capacity,” Musa said. “We’re blocking the logistics and taking them out from within Nigeria.” The post 2027: US providing real-time intelligence to Nigerian military against terrorists — Musa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Obi highlights institutional reforms during Anambra tenure
item.description: Former Anambra State Governor and the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has highlighted the institutional reforms undertaken by his administration, saying rebuilding the machinery of government was essential to achieving sustainable development. Obi disclosed this on Tuesday in the second instalment of his series, titled Nigerians, Go and Verify, published on his X handle. In the article, titled Building the Institutions of the State, the former governor explained that his administration prioritised strengthening government institutions under the Anambra Integrated Development Strategy, ANIDS, before embarking on broader development projects. He said his administration was guided by the principles of character, competence, capacity and compassion, adding that a development vision could not succeed without strong institutions to implement it. According to him, the physical and administrative structures of governance were in deplorable condition when he assumed office, making it necessary to rebuild institutions across the executive, legislature, judiciary, civil service and local government system. Restoring the seat of government Obi said his administration rebuilt, re-equipped and furnished the Government House in Awka after it was vandalised and burnt in 2004. He added that the Governor’s Lodge in Amawbia was rehabilitated, while a new Governor’s Lodge was constructed in Onitsha to strengthen executive presence and facilitate governance across the state’s major administrative and commercial centres. Strengthening the legislature and judiciary The former governor said his administration also rehabilitated the Anambra State House of Assembly Complex in Awka and provided vehicles to lawmakers to facilitate the discharge of their legislative responsibilities. He said the judiciary was equally strengthened through the provision of brand-new vehicles to High Court judges, which he described as the first of its kind in the state’s history. Obi also said vehicles were provided to magistrates for the first time since the creation of Anambra State. He explained that the interventions were aimed at improving mobility, strengthening the administration of justice and enabling judicial officers to perform their duties more effectively. Rebuilding the civil service On the civil service, Obi said many Ministries, Departments and Agencies, MDAs, operated from scattered rented apartments before his administration, while civil servants lacked a centralised and decent working environment. He said the arrangement undermined administrative coordination, efficiency and the dignity of public service. To address the situation, he said his administration constructed the two-phase Chief Jerome Udoji State Secretariat Complex, comprising Blocks 1 and 2, to bring the MDAs together and provide civil servants with a more conducive working environment. item.title: FG introduces NIN-linked verification system for domestic air passengers
item.description: The Federal Government has introduced a biometric passenger verification system linked to the National Identification Number (NIN) for domestic air travel, in a move aimed at strengthening airport security and curbing identity fraud. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Tuesday after unveiling the Airport Passenger Verification System, known as V-PASS, at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos. Keyamo said the system would make it mandatory for passengers on domestic flights to verify their identities using their NIN before boarding. He explained that the technology was designed to eliminate cases of passengers travelling with fake identities, as well as address touting and ticket racketeering at airports. According to him, the biometric identity verification system would enhance passenger processing, strengthen airport security and provide a faster and more seamless travel experience. The minister said the project was executed through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) arrangement. He was accompanied at the unveiling by the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Mrs Olubunmi Kuku; Director-General of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC), Dr Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh; and other senior FAAN officials. Keyamo said he had directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) to give all airlines operating in the country until December 31 to integrate with the system. He clarified that the verification system was designed exclusively for domestic flights. item.title: Tinubu: Nigerians can access ₦100m mortgages at 9.75%
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has said eligible Nigerians can access mortgage loans of up to ₦100 million at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent under the Federal Government’s ₦1 trillion MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF). Tinubu, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Tuesday, said the initiative was designed to expand access to affordable, long-term housing finance and help more Nigerians become homeowners. He explained that beneficiaries could repay the loans over a period of up to 20 years, with an initial deposit of 10 per cent. Illustrating the arrangement, the President said a Nigerian seeking to purchase a house worth ₦10 million would need an initial deposit of ₦1 million and could repay approximately ₦85,400 monthly over 20 years. According to him, more than 2,300 Nigerians across 27 states have so far accessed ₦160 billion in mortgages through MREIF. Tinubu said the Federal Government had also strengthened the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN), through which eligible Nigerians could access housing loans of up to ₦50 million at six per cent interest, with repayment periods of up to 30 years. He added that contributors to pension schemes could qualify to use up to 25 per cent of their retirement savings towards the initial deposit, while married applicants could submit joint applications with their spouses to improve their chances of accessing higher loan amounts. The President also highlighted the role of the Family Homes Fund in providing affordable housing for Nigerians who cannot afford mortgage arrangements. He said the fund had delivered more than 53 social homes for vulnerable and underserved households. Tinubu further disclosed that the Renewed Hope Social Housing Programme was targeting 77,400 affordable homes across the country. According to him, 100 free homes had been delivered to widows in Kaduna, while another 50 were provided to wives of fallen military personnel in Ibadan. He added that more than 15,000 housing units were under construction nationwide through the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme. The President stressed that access to the housing initiatives should be based on eligibility rather than political connections or religious affiliation. “You should not need to know a minister, a governor or anybody in the Presidential Villa to apply and benefit from these opportunities,” he said. Tinubu maintained that the programmes were open to Nigerians who met the stipulated requirements, irrespective of their location or beliefs. He said providing opportunities for hardworking Nigerians to own homes and secure their families’ future remained an important objective of his administration’s economic reforms. item.title: Enugu Assembly passes bill limiting rent increase to 2%
item.description: … Landlords can only review rent after four years By Chinedu Adonu The Enugu State House of Assembly has passed a bill seeking to protect tenants from arbitrary rent increases by restricting landlords to a maximum two per cent increment every four years. The bill, which scaled its third reading on Tuesday, also provides for a maximum 10 per cent rent increase where a landlord has undertaken reasonable renovation of the property. Its passage followed the consideration of a report presented by a joint House committee comprising the Committees on Housing and Investment, Public Petition, Ethics and Privileges, and Judiciary. The motion for consideration of the report was moved by the member representing Nkanu West Constituency, Hon. Iloabuchi Aniagu, and seconded by the member representing Awgu North Constituency, Rt. Hon. Jane Eneh. Presenting the report, Chairman of the Committee, Rt. Hon. Okey Mbah, who represents Nkanu East Constituency, said the proposed amendment followed extensive consultations with relevant stakeholders. Mbah described the legislation as a major intervention in landlord-tenant relations, saying it was designed to address the exploitation of tenants and ease the burden of securing accommodation in the state. “This bill will subside over 60 per cent of what residents used to pay while trying to secure accommodation,” he said. Following the presentation, the House dissolved into the Committee of the Whole to consider the report alongside the bill before its eventual passage. The Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Uche Ugwu, described the legislation as part of the good governance initiatives of the present administration, saying it would give tenants in the state a new lease of life. The bill, titled A Bill for a Law to Amend the Landlord and Tenant Second Amendment Bill, Cap 101, Revised Laws of Enugu State 2024, House Bill No. 3, 2025, passed second reading on March 11, 2026, and subsequently underwent a public hearing on March 26, 2026. With its passage by the Assembly, the bill now awaits the assent of Governor Peter Mbah before it can become law. item.title: Car washer jailed seven years for stealing customer’s Lexus SUV in Enugu
item.description: By Alumona Ukwueze ENUGU—-A 36-year-old car washer, Adah Martins Pius, has been sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment for stealing a customer’s Toyota Lexus 330 SUV in Enugu State. The Enugu State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Daniel Ndukwe. According to the statement, Pius stole the black Lexus SUV on November 5, 2026, after it was entrusted to him by its owner for washing at Fourth Dimension, Enugu. Rather than wash and return the vehicle, the convict, a native of Ugep in Yakurr Local Government Area of Cross River State, allegedly absconded with it and fled to his hometown. Following a complaint by the vehicle’s owner, operatives of the New Haven Police Division deployed technical intelligence to track down and arrest him in Cross River State. The stolen SUV was subsequently recovered on November 11, 2026. The police said Pius was arraigned before the Enugu North Magistrate Court on November 16, 2026, on a one-count charge of stealing. He pleaded guilty to the charge and was convicted and sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment by the court. The Command commended the operatives involved in the investigation and arrest, as well as the court for the speedy dispensation of justice. It reiterated its commitment to sustaining efforts to rid Enugu State of criminal elements and ensure the safety of residents and their property. The post Car washer jailed seven years for stealing customer’s Lexus SUV in Enugu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ikeja LG chairman mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Executive Chairman of Ikeja Local Government, Comrade Akeem Olalekan Dauda, popularly known as AKOD, has commiserated with Vanguard Media Limited, the family and associates of its late Online Editor, Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa. Dauda described Ajasa’s death as a painful loss to the media industry and the journalism profession. Ajasa, aged 44, reportedly died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness. In a condolence message, the council chairman said the late journalist’s dedication, professionalism and contributions to the growth of digital journalism would remain part of his enduring legacy. He described Ajasa as a committed media professional whose career across several reputable media organisations reflected his passion for journalism, pursuit of excellence and determination to contribute to the evolving media landscape. Dauda particularly commiserated with the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the immediate family of the deceased, as well as his friends and professional colleagues. He urged them to take solace in the impactful life and professional contributions of the late journalist. “Take solace in the impactful life and professional contributions of the late Ajasa, whose passing at the age of 44 is a painful reminder of the fragility of life,” he stated. The council chairman also prayed that Almighty God would comfort the bereaved family, grant them the strength to bear the loss and give the deceased eternal rest. The post Ikeja LG chairman mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Ijaw people support Tinubu’s re-election, Diri declares
item.description: ..Commends Tompolo-led campaign movement …Group donates 25 buses for campaign By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa Bayelsa State Governor, Douye Diri, has declared that the majority of Ijaw people support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. Diri said he was confident that the Ijaw nation would give Tinubu overwhelming support in the election, describing the President and the people of the Niger Delta as being in the same political boat. The governor spoke during a rally organised by the High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, led PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital. He said the Ijaw people, being experienced mariners and navigators, would ensure that the political boat sailed to victory. Diri listed the ongoing construction of the second phase of the Nembe-Brass Road, tax waivers granted to the state’s independent power plant and the coastal highway project among the benefits he said Bayelsa had received under Tinubu’s administration. He also commended Tompolo for his commitment to Tinubu’s re-election campaign, describing his involvement in a nationwide presidential campaign as a source of pride to the Ijaw people. “This is the first time an Ijaw son is carrying a presidential campaign across states on this scale. As a people who have over the years talked about injustice and recognition, we are proud of Tompolo,” he said. The governor also thanked the movement’s leader for donating 25 vehicles to support the President’s campaign in Bayelsa. Diri, while dismissing claims that a particular political party was the Ijaw party, said the All Progressives Congress (APC) was the party to which he, Tompolo and other prominent Ijaw people belonged. According to him, “The real Ijaw party in Nigeria is the APC, to which I, as Governor-General of the Ijaw nation, Tompolo and other prominent Ijaw sons and daughters belong.” Earlier, the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Limited, Kestin Pondi, who represented Tompolo, said the visit was to inaugurate the Bayelsa State chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement. Pondi acknowledged Diri’s role in the President’s re-election campaign and expressed confidence in the collaboration between the governor and the movement. He described Tinubu as a bold and courageous leader who had prioritised Nigeria in his reform agenda, arguing that the President deserved another term to consolidate the gains of his administration. item.title: Simon Ekpa freed from Finnish custody, Ejimakor announces
item.description: Nigerian-born separatist leader, Simon Ekpa, has been freed from custody in Finland, according to a Nigerian lawyer, Aloy Ejimakor. Ejimakor disclosed this on his Facebook page on Tuesday, saying he received confirmation of Ekpa’s release from his close friend and ally, Dr David Matsanga. “ Mazi SIMON EKPA has just been FREED. His close friend and ally, Dr David Matsanga, confirmed it to me just minutes ago during our telephone conversation,” Ejimakor wrote. The announcement comes amid earlier reports that Ekpa was scheduled to be released on November 17, 2026. His legal support team had previously confirmed the date, following the circulation of a viral video purportedly showing him walking out of a building said to be the facility where he was being detained. Ekpa, 41, had been in Finnish custody since November 2024. He was convicted in September 2025 by the Päijät-Häme District Court over his alleged involvement in activities linked to armed separatist groups operating in southeastern Nigeria. The post Simon Ekpa freed from Finnish custody, Ejimakor announces appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: $4.5m car theft: Canadian police arrest eight Nigerians, four others
item.description: By Matthew Johnson Peel Regional Police, Canada, has arrested eight Nigerians among 12 suspects following the dismantling of a transnational auto theft syndicate allegedly shipping stolen luxury vehicles to West Africa. The suspects, who are facing a combined 231 criminal charges, were nabbed after detectives with the Commercial Auto Crime Bureau recovered 96 stolen high-value vehicles, predominantly luxury sport utility vehicles, SUVs, and pickup trucks valued at approximately $4.5 million. In a video posted on its official X (formerly Twitter) handle on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, the Peel Regional Police disclosed that the investigation, code-named Project Cadetta, was launched in March 2026 in collaboration with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA). According to the police, the operation initially focused on a warehouse in Brampton, Ontario, which served as a primary staging facility where stolen vehicles with altered Vehicle Identification Numbers (re-VINed) were concealed inside shipping containers destined for West African markets through Canadian ports. Further investigations uncovered a broader criminal network operating across the Greater Toronto Area (GTA) and surrounding jurisdictions. Police alleged that the syndicate was spearheaded by five principal suspects—all bearing Nigerian names who coordinated the theft, movement, and overseas export of the vehicles. They were identified as Odewale Abraham (57), Tosin Oyebade (45), Oluyemi Sodade (51), and Oluwaseyi Bameke (39), all of Toronto, alongside Stanley Udeh (46) of Brampton. Seven other suspects accused of facilitating the racket through transportation, container movements, and managing loading sites were identified as Gbolahan Babatunde (29) of Vaughan; Olushola Oke (42) of Toronto; Kenneth Okafor (58) of no fixed address; Karamveer Singh (26) of Brampton; Darryl Davance (25) of Saint Jerome, Quebec; Henrik Gancz (57) of no fixed address; and Jaspreet Singh (25) of no fixed address. Following a series of coordinated search warrants and arrests, nine of the accused were charged and released with future court dates, while three were held for bail hearings and subsequently granted release. Canadian authorities disclosed that some of the charged suspects may be referred to the CBSA for immigration enforcement action, including possible deportation from Canada, upon the conclusion of their criminal trials. Meanwhile, arrest warrants have been issued for two additional suspects still at large: 32-year-old Steven Gyamfi and a 16-year-old minor from Hamilton whose identity is protected under Canada’s Youth Criminal Justice Act. Commenting on the breakthrough, Deputy Chief of Peel Regional Police, Nick Milinovich, vowed that the force would sustain its clampdown on organised crime syndicates. “Organised auto theft is a predatory business model run by transnational syndicates that terrorise families and fund broader criminal enterprises. item.title: Singapore In Damage Control After Nvidia Scandal Exposes China Loophole
item.description: Singapore is working to maintain its reputation as a trusted business hub, tainted by allegations that Chinese companies had exploited it to gain access to top-end AI chips despite US export restrictions. A widening scandal sparked by an affair between Jensen Huang, until recently head of US chip titan Nvidia, and a suspected Chinese spy has spotlighted the city-state’s position as a global crossroads for the advanced semiconductors that power artificial intelligence. This screengrab from video footage by CTI obtained via AFPTV on November 9, 2026 shows Alice Huang (R), a Chinese executive linked to the data centre company called Megaspeed, attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (L in black back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP The United States on Monday moved to close a loophole in its controls — which it says protect national security — on the export of powerful AI chips to China. The new US rules crack down on illicit chip smuggling, but also the large grey market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres full of advanced Nvidia chips in third countries, often in Southeast Asia. It follows explosive reports of Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International, which Washington is investigating for the alleged transfer of Nvidia chips to China in circumvention of US rules. The scandal “is obviously not a good look for Singapore”, Chong Ja Ian, a political scientist with the National University of Singapore, told AFP. Singapore is also probing what Megaspeed was up to, but Chong said the city-state must strengthen regulatory oversight to avoid the perception of “systemic issues”. Map of Singapore The Nvidia case may make it harder “to maintain the reputation of being a clean business hub by simply dealing with individual cases, rather than putting more stringent regulations and laws in place”, he said. Some US officials also reportedly believe that Alice Huang, no relation to the leather jacket-clad Jensen, was spying for Beijing. Caught in crossfire? Singapore said it was carefully studying the new US measures, which require data centres worldwide to hold a US licence to provide a large volume of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, or other places under US arms embargoes. A US licence will also be needed to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil — countries the US Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” of the sensitive components. “We take our international reputation seriously,” the Singaporean government said. item.title: Reno Omokri mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: Former presidential aide and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Mexico, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua, Bemigho Reno Omokri, has mourned the passing of Vanguard Newspapers’ Online Editor, Mr Femi Ajasa, describing his death as a loss to Nigerian journalism. Omokri, in a condolence message posted on his Facebook page on Tuesday, said Ajasa embodied the Omoluabi principle and demonstrated professionalism, ethical conduct and commitment to excellence in journalism. He said he had known the late journalist personally, recalling that Ajasa extended a hand of fellowship to him during his lifetime. “On behalf of my family and I, please accept my condolences on the death of your staff member, Online Editor Femi Ajasa. “I knew Mr Ajasa, and he truly embodied the Omoluabi principle. He extended his right hand of fellowship to me in his lifetime, and it is a sad day for Nigerian journalism that he is no more,” he said. The ambassador described Ajasa as a model of high-level reporting, drawing a comparison between his journalistic standards and those of Vanguard’s founder, Mr Sam Amuka. He also credited Ajasa’s dedication to journalism and pursuit of excellence with contributing to Vanguard’s prominence in online publishing. According to him, the late editor’s professional ethics and insight had created a vacuum that would be difficult to fill. “The vacuum that Mr Ajasa’s passing has created will be difficult to fill because of the ethics and insight he brought to his job,” Omokri said. He prayed for the repose of Ajasa’s soul and asked that his memory remain blessed. “May his soul rest in peace and his memory be forever blessed,” he added. The post Reno Omokri mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: APC zones Bayelsa West Senate seat to Ekeremor
item.description: …Reserves Reps seat for Sagbama, insists on rotation By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa YENAGOA — Critical stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Bayelsa West Senatorial District have reaffirmed their commitment to the existing power-sharing arrangement between Sagbama and Ekeremor Local Government Areas, insisting that Ekeremor should produce the next senator while Sagbama takes the House of Representatives seat. The stakeholders also resolved to mobilise support for all APC candidates, from President Bola Tinubu to the State House of Assembly, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The resolutions were reached at the APC Bayelsa West stakeholders’ meeting in Yenagoa, where party leaders reiterated their commitment to the rotation arrangement, which they said was designed to promote fairness, unity and political balance between the two local government areas. Speaking at the meeting, the Deputy Governor, Dr Peter Akpe, urged party members to unite, reconcile their differences and intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the elections. Akpe, who is from the senatorial district, restated Governor Douye Diri’s charge to APC members to work towards an overwhelming victory in 2027, stressing that the party should aim to secure more than 75 per cent of the votes in every polling unit. He also urged the party’s candidates to extend a hand of fellowship to members who did not support them during the primaries, saying the election presented an opportunity to rebuild relationships within the party. “I think we have passed the stage of saying this man or woman should not have been the candidate. We have moved past that time. “They might not have been the best among us, but know that in the business of selection, there is always the God factor. At this point, we all have to sink our differences and work for the success of our party,” he said. Akpe urged members to regard the election as a collective responsibility, noting that voters would identify the party by its name and symbol on the ballot. He particularly appealed to the candidates to reach out to aggrieved members rather than wait for them to initiate reconciliation. “To the candidates, you really have to extend your arm of fellowship. Don’t say this person supported me and that person did not. Reach out to everybody and don’t wait for the other person to do it. You are the one to do it,” he admonished. The Deputy Governor also cautioned members against undermining party leaders, stressing that electoral success required cooperation and collective effort. Also speaking, the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, challenged APC leaders in the district to work towards delivering all the votes for Tinubu and other party candidates in 2027. item.title: NDLEA busts Sahara-Europe cocaine syndicate, arrests eight
item.description: …Suspects excrete 634 cocaine pellets weighing 13.8kg … Cartel planned smuggling route through Niger, Libya By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, NDLEA, have dismantled a suspected transnational cocaine trafficking syndicate allegedly operating a smuggling route from Lagos through northern Nigeria and across the Sahara Desert into Europe, arresting eight suspected drug couriers in coordinated operations in Lagos and Kano. The suspects were arrested between October 30 and 31, 2026, following intelligence-led operations, while a combined total of 634 wraps of cocaine weighing 13.795 kilogrammes were recovered after they excreted the drugs in custody. NDLEA Chairman, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), on Tuesday commended operatives of the agency’s commands for their collaboration and professionalism, saying their coordination prevented the suspects from escaping between Lagos and Kano. “This cartel thought it had found a back door to Europe through our northern borders and the Sahara. Their arrests are a message to drug barons and their couriers that there is no safe route out of Nigeria. Whether they go by air, by road, or through the desert, we will trace them, find them, and bring them to justice,” Marwa said. He cautioned young Nigerians against serving as drug couriers, warning that ingesting narcotics could have fatal consequences. “Swallowing wraps of cocaine is a death wish. One burst pellet can kill a mule before the journey ends. No amount of money is worth that risk,” he added. The agency’s Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, said the operation began on October 30 when operatives of the Special Operations Unit arrested a 57-year-old suspect, Okwudiba Ifeanyichukwu Damian, at a hotel in the Ago Palace area of Okota, Lagos. Babafemi said Damian subsequently excreted 74 wraps of cocaine weighing 1.650 kilogrammes under observation. He disclosed that on October 31, operatives intercepted four other suspects at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, MM2, Lagos, as they prepared to board a flight to Kano. item.title: Fountain of Life Church rejects Jimmy Odukoya’s removal
item.description: The Fountain of Life Church has rejected reports alleging that Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has been removed as its Senior Pastor, describing the purported decision as constitutionally invalid. The church, in a statement issued on Tuesday, said the announcement did not represent a valid decision of the Board of Trustees of The Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church. “Our attention has been drawn to media reports alleging that Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has been removed as Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church. “We categorically reject this purported decision and wish to clarify that the announcement does not represent a constitutionally valid decision of the Board of Trustees of The Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church,” the statement read. The church said the announcement reflected the position of some individuals who had constituted themselves into a group known as the “Concerned Members of the Board”. It accused the group of acting outside the constitutional framework governing the church. The statement further disclosed that the trustees involved had been formally asked to resign from the board on March 14, 2026, over alleged repeated violations of the church’s constitution and founding principles. “It is important to place on record that, as far back as 14 March 2026, these Trustees were formally called upon to resign from the Board on account of their repeated and flagrant violations of the Church’s Constitution and its founding principles and objectives,” it said. According to the church, the communication was delivered to and acknowledged by the trustees, while one of them subsequently resigned. It alleged that the remaining individuals had continued to take decisions purportedly binding on the church without complying with its governing constitution. Reaffirming Odukoya’s position, the church insisted that he remained its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees. “For the avoidance of doubt, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya remains the duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees of The Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church,” the statement added. It said his appointment was unanimously approved by the board in September 2023, stressing that no constitutionally valid decision had been taken to remove him from either position. “The Constitution remains the governing instrument of the Church. No individual or group of individuals can substitute their preferences for the express provisions of that Constitution,” it stated. The church urged its members, the media and the general public to distinguish between the pronouncements of the individuals involved and what it described as its constitutionally authorised position. item.title: Breaking: Omotosho, Nwite, 10 others sworn in as Appeal Court Justices
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, on Tuesday swore in 12 new Justices of the Court of Appeal. Among the new appellate court justices whose elevation the National Judicial Council (NJC) recommended at its meeting on May 13 are two Federal High Court judges, Justices James Omotosho and Emeka Nwite, who hitherto handled high-profile cases. Justice Omotosho had on November 20, 2025, convicted and sentenced the detained leader of the proscribed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), Nnamdi Kanu, to life imprisonment after finding him guilty on a seven-count terrorism-related charge that the federal government filed against him. Likewise, Justice Nwite, who is handling the N80.2 billion fraud case against the immediate past Governor of Kogi State, Alhaji Yahaya Bello, had on June 3 convicted and sentenced four members of the Al-Shabaab terrorist group to death by hanging for their roles in the June 5, 2022 attack on St. Francis Catholic Church in Owo, Ondo States. Meanwhile, the other justices also sworn in to the appellate court bench by the CJN on Tuesday are Justices Yakubu Abdulhammeed Mohammed, Abodunde Monisola Oluwatoyin, Ajuwa Raphael, Abua Elias Ojie, Ijohor Mbalamen Jennifer, Shuaibu Sabiu Bala, Buba Dauda Njane, Kado Sanusi, Ademola Enikuomehin and Dadom Julcit Veronica. All criminal cases previously before the judges, including the trial of former Governor Bello, will be reassigned to another judge of the court and heard de-novo (afresh). In her address at the occasion, the CJN said the appointments of the new justices brought together “judicial experience from different parts of the country and from courts with distinct jurisdictions and responsibilities.” She disclosed that some of the justices were selected from Gombe, Bayelsa, Cross River, Benue, Kebbi, Taraba and Ondo, following their service at the High Court, the National Industrial Court and the Customary Courts of Appeal in Ekiti and Plateau states. She urged the justices to be mindful that, unlike before when they presided over cases alone, their new assignment would require them to sit with other justices in panels, deliberate collectively and arrive at decisions through a process of judicial engagement. “Your responsibility, therefore, extends beyond determining whether a decision should be affirmed or set aside. You are called upon to promote consistency in the application of the law, clarify legal principles, correct errors where necessary and contribute to the coherent development of our jurisprudence. “This requires a disciplined and principled approach to appellate adjudication. “An appeal is not an invitation to rehear a case simply because another judicial officer might have reached a different conclusion. item.title: Abia records 60% drop in maternal deaths — Govt
item.description: …Renovates 190 PHCs, functionalises 123 …Nursing college gets increased admission quota By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Abia State Government has announced a 60 per cent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026, saying the state now has the second-lowest maternal mortality rate in the country. The government attributed the reported improvement to ongoing reforms in the health sector, including the rehabilitation of primary healthcare centres and increased investment in healthcare delivery. Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this during a briefing on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting at Government House, Umuahia. He was represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Ferdinand Ekeoma. Kanu said the administration had made progress in its efforts to revitalise primary healthcare, disclosing that 190 of the 200 primary healthcare centres earmarked for renovation under Project Ekwueme had been completed. He said 123 of the renovated facilities had been made functional to provide essential medical services, while 27 had been equipped with solar power, with work ongoing at nine additional centres. The Commissioner also announced the completion of all 77 World Bank-supported health projects in the state. In another development, Kanu disclosed that the Aba Campus of the College of Nursing Sciences had secured an increase in its admission quota from 75 to 120 students following an accreditation exercise by the National Nursing and Midwifery Council. According to him, the revised admission quota was communicated in an accreditation report released on November 13, reflecting the outcome of the institution’s accreditation exercise. Meanwhile, the Rector of Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, Dr Christopher Okoro, has emerged Administrator of the Year in a nationwide poll organised by Leadership Excellence Award. Kanu said Okoro secured 148,267 votes in the exercise, which recognised his contributions to institutional development, human capital development and technical and professional education. He attributed the recognition to developments recorded at the institution under the Rector, including an increase in student enrolment by more than 6,000, improved infrastructure and better staff welfare. The Commissioner also said the state government remained committed to education development, noting that the sector continued to receive 20 per cent of the state’s annual budget. On public health surveillance, the government reported that Abia recorded no cases of Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera, mpox or yellow fever during the period under review. The Commissioner for Health, Prof. Enoch Ogbonnaya Uche, who also addressed the briefing, provided an update on the Ebola situation in the country. item.title: Pope calls for ‘less division’ after US midterm elections
item.description: Pope Leo XIV on Tuesday voiced hope for “less war” and “less division” following the midterm elections in his native United States, as he returned from a tour of South America. The first American pope has clashed repeatedly with US President Donald Trump over the war with Iran and made history this month by announcing that he had cast a ballot in the midterms — the first time a pope has been known to have voted. “I would like to see a greater capacity for dialogue, for building bridges, for reconciliation. Less polemics, less war, less division,” the US-born pontiff told reporters including AFP on the papal plane. “I know this is also a dream, but I know it is possible so we shall see,” he said. Trump’s Republican party was handed a resounding defeat in the midterms in large part due to anger over soaring energy prices and the president’s costly war with Iran. – ‘Seeds of hope’ – Leo’s comments echoed his repeated calls for an end to polarisation during his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. The visit, which came less than a month after the 71-year-old underwent lung cancer surgery, also highlighted the social justice priorities shaping his papacy. From the high Andes to the sweltering Amazon, Leo crisscrossed a continent where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary, picking up Peruvian citizenship along the way. Visiting care homes and prisons, the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics reminded political leaders like Argentina’s Javier Milei that economic growth must benefit all, speaking in defence of the poor, the elderly and disabled people. In a lighter moment, the pope joked with reporters about being hit in the face with a rosary bracelet thrown from the crowd as he arrived for a mass in Lima. “The affection of Peruvians — including that person who, with great faith, simply wanted to offer me a rosary — these are things one carries in one’s heart, perhaps in one’s eye,” he said. Asked about his apparent criticism of Milei, he said his comments about Argentina’s austerity policies were “not political” but he encouraged the Argentine leader “to take greater account above all of those most in need”. “I hope that once again we’ve sown seeds of hope, a message of the possibility of unity despite difficulties and differences,” he said. Leo also applied his message of unity to the Catholic Church, which saw periods of factionalism under his predecessor Pope Francis. “What I believe is important in my ministry to the Church is to bring healing, to bring people together. “First let us come together, let us consider what we think the priorities must be, and then we will see how we move forward from there,” he said. – No resignation letter – The visit went ahead exactly as planned despite doubts among many observers after the pope’s surgery on October 13 in which part of his right lung was removed. item.title: Drones Behind Nearly 75% Of Civilian Deaths This Year In Sudan War — UN
item.description: Drones caused nearly three quarters of all the verified civilian fatalities this year in the war in Sudan, the UN said Tuesday. The war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) erupted in April 2023 and is estimated to have killed more than 200,000 people in total. The conflict has forced more than 13 million to flee their homes, creating the world’s largest hunger and displacement crisis, according to aid groups. A young displaced Sudanese girl reacts after spending a night with others in Gedaref city, eastern Sudan, on December 26, 2025, after the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) took control of the Heglig area in western Sudan. (Photo by AFP) Out of 2,230 civilian deaths confirmed by the UN human rights office OHCHR to have occurred this year between January and the end of October, more than 1,630 were a result of drone attacks, it said on Tuesday. Drone attacks have “eclipsed the use of other tactics and weaponry”, it said, adding that the full civilian casualty figures are likely to be higher. A Sudanese woman who fled El-Fasher sits next to aid she received at the Al-Afad camp for displaced people in the town of Al-Dabba, northern Sudan, on November 25, 2025. (Photo by Ebrahim HAMID / AFP) Both warring parties have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away. In a report on the human rights situation in Sudan, OHCHR said the first six months of the year were marked by an “unmistakable increase in drone strikes against civilians and civilian objects”. The use of drones has now become “one of the defining features of the conflict”, it said. With the war well into its fourth year, “a robust war economy and steady supply of weapons and other external support enabled the parties to sustain fighting as the conflict continued to spread and evolve,” the report said. The conflict is exacting an “unbearable toll” on civilians, while the prospects for a ceasefire and a peaceful resolution to the conflict remain elusive, it said. Ali Muhammad Ali Abd al-Rahman, a Sudanese national, waits to hear the verdict of the International Criminal Court (ICC), in The Hague, on December 9, 2025. The International Criminal Court on December 9, 2025, handed down a sentence of 20 years to a Sudanese militia leader for war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during the country’s civil war two decades ago. item.title: Deputy Senate President mourns late Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau I. Jibrin, has mourned the passing of Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, the Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers. Mr Ajasa passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness at the age of 44, according to the management of Vanguard Media Limited, publishers of the Vanguard Newspapers. In a condolence message issued by his spokesperson, Ismail Mudashir, Senator Barau described the late Ajasa as a thoroughbred professional and one of the finest minds in Nigeria’s digital journalism space. “Femi Ajasa’s dedication and commitment to truth and accuracy set him apart and distinguished him among others. His death is a painful loss, not only to his immediate family, the Vanguard family, but to the entire Nigerian media industry,” he said. The Deputy President of the Senate noted that Mr Ajasa’s journalism journey, which began as a photojournalist with the National Mirror in 2012, through TheNewsGuru and Pulse, to his return to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, was marked by excellence, integrity and selfless service to the country through his noble profession, journalism. Senator Barau extended his heartfelt condolences to the Ajasa family of Ajido, Badagry, Lagos State, Management and Staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) and all his friends and professional associates. “We pray that God will grant his family, colleagues and loved ones the strength and fortitude to bear this irreparable loss, and grant his gentle soul eternal rest,” he said. item.title: Bangladesh Garment Workers, Police Clash In Fresh Wage Protest
item.description: Bangladeshi police fired tear gas and stun grenades on Tuesday in clashes with thousands of garment workers who were protesting after a key wage board meeting was postponed. Protesters hurled bricks, torched vehicles, and blocked the main highway between the capital, Dhaka, and the key financial district of Mymensingh as demonstrations over wage conditions turned violent. The South Asian nation of 170 million people is the world’s second-biggest garment exporter behind China, producing clothes for major international brands including Fruit of the Loom and Levi Strauss. A garment worker throws back a tear gas cannister during a protest demanding increase in minimum wages, in Gazipur city on the outskirts of Dhaka on November 17, 2026. Photo by MD ABU SUFIAN JEWEL / AFP But growing worker unrest over wages that began in October has threatened to disrupt the industry that generates $38 billion in revenues annually and employs more than four million people. Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($240) — a 140-percent increase on the current 12,500 taka, as they struggle to cope with rising food, housing, transport and healthcare costs. Garment workers shout slogans and block roads during a protest demanding increase in minimum wages, in Gazipur city on the outskirts of Dhaka on November 17, 2026. Photo by MD ABU SUFIAN JEWEL / AFP Some 500 factories out of 4,500 are currently shut, sources told AFP, something that is further stoking unrest among workers. “The owners seem unwilling to meet our salary demands. They are already dragging their feet,” said Khanom, 24, who gave only one name. Garment workers look on from a bridge during a protest demanding increase in minimum wages, in Gazipur city on the outskirts of Dhaka on November 17, 2026. Photo by MD ABU SUFIAN JEWEL / AFP In a joint statement, the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) called for a resumption of wage negotiations as soon as possible. The disruption comes during the run-up to Christmas, the busiest export period for Bangladesh’s garment industry. item.title: Why Nigeria’s Credit Market Must Finance Both the Buyer and the Seller
item.description: Credit plays an important role in keeping economic activity moving. For many households, access to credit makes it possible to spread the cost of major purchases over time rather than pay the full amount upfront. This improves purchasing power, supports household consumption and creates demand for businesses across different sectors. When individuals can afford to make purchases, businesses have more opportunities to sell their products and services. However, financing buyers alone is not enough to drive economic growth. The businesses that supply these goods and services also need access to credit to purchase inventory, pay suppliers, manage operating costs and fulfil orders. Supporting both consumers and merchants requires lenders to recognise that the two groups have different financing needs and cannot be assessed in the same way. Lenders must understand these differences when determining how much to lend, the appropriate repayment terms and the risks involved. Chukwuma Nwanze, Managing Director of Credit Direct , highlighted this distinction during a panel discussion at Moonshot. He explained that while lenders assess an individual’s earnings, disposable income, existing financial obligations, and borrowing behaviour, evaluating merchants requires a closer look at their cash flow, turnover, and business growth. A credit market that serves only one side of this relationship risks leaving important parts of the economy underserved. For many businesses, the ability to meet demand depends on having enough working capital. Merchants need funds to purchase inventory, pay suppliers, manage operating expenses and fulfil customer orders. These costs often arise before revenue from sales is received, creating a gap between the money a business needs to operate and the money coming into it. This challenge can become more evident when demand increases. A business may have an opportunity to serve more customers but lack the funds to purchase additional stock or expand its capacity. Delayed access to financing can therefore limit its ability to respond to market opportunities, even when there is a clear demand for its products. Working capital financing can help businesses manage these gaps and maintain the flow of goods and services. It can also give merchants greater flexibility to plan inventory purchases, meet supplier obligations and sustain operations through periods of uneven cash flow. The importance of merchant financing becomes clearer when considered alongside consumer credit. Financing customers’ purchases creates demand for a product, and financing merchants gives businesses the resources to meet that demand. This, therefore, builds a credit market that contributes meaningfully to economic growth. Merchant assessment requires a closer examination of business performance.
